text: "After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up." With the Lord a day is as a thousand years.
explanation:
Peter gives a key for reading prophetic days: "With the Lord one day is as a thousand years." About two thousand years have passed since Jesus came. We're the generation living after the two days, early on the third. And Jesus rose early in the morning on the third day.

The word revive means to restore to life. Before He raises us up to "live in His sight," face to face, expect God to pour out restoration and health, even as the world struggles with diseases old and new. Earlier generations longed to see this hour. You're living in it.

text: The early rain is moreh, from the same root as "teacher." The latter rain, malkosh, ripens the harvest. Both come from God.
explanation:
In Israel, the former rain falls around October and November, just after sowing; it makes the seed sprout. The latter rain comes in spring and fills out the grain for harvest. Moreh, the early rain, comes from the same Hebrew root as teacher: good teaching falls on hearts like refreshing rain.

There are seasons in your life too. Sometimes you sense God's presence and hear His Word, yet see no visible results. That's sowing time; the seed is germinating. Don't give up. "The farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, waiting patiently for it until it receives the early and latter rain." Harvest comes in its season.

text: Jesus stayed two days with the Samaritans, then went to Cana, where He'd turned water into wine "on the third day."
explanation:
John keeps pointing to the pattern. "On the third day there was a wedding in Cana." After the Samaritan woman's town welcomed Him, Jesus "stayed there two days" with these non-Jews, then returned to Cana in Galilee. When Lazarus was dying, He "stayed two more days" across the Jordan, then said, "Let us go to Judea again."

For about two thousand years, Jesus has largely been the Bread of Life to the Gentile world. He has never stopped loving Israel, and now He's turning back to them too. And the next great event for the church is a wedding: the marriage supper of the Lamb.

text: The Jordan didn't part while the priests watched from the bank. It parted when their feet touched the water.
explanation:
It was harvest time and the Jordan was overflowing its banks, a torrent no one could swim. Israel camped beside it for three days. God didn't divide the river while they waited or while they walked toward it. "As soon as the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark… shall rest in the waters of the Jordan… the waters shall be cut off."

God rarely gives grace in advance of the need. The soldier doesn't feel tomorrow's courage today. If you're dreading tomorrow's meeting, diagnosis or decision, don't panic that you don't feel strong enough yet. Step forward in faith. The supply comes when you're face to face with the need. "Sufficient for the day is its own trouble."

text: "He will without fail drive out… the Canaanites and the Hittites." One name relates to trading; the other to terror.
explanation:
Before Israel crossed the Jordan, Joshua promised that God would drive out seven nations. Scripture often hides lessons in names. Canaanite has been linked with merchants and trading: the mindset of bartering with God, "If I do this, You'll do that." Grace drives that out; you can't trade with God, because everything you have came from Him.

Hittite is associated with chet, a root meaning terror or dread. Whatever your fear is, whether of the night, of losing a child, or of not having enough, God promises to drive it out "without fail." These enemies are trespassers in the land He has given you.

text: Hivites can suggest squatters, Perizzites unwalled villages, Jebusites being trodden down. God drives them all out.
explanation:
Has something moved into an area of your life that doesn't belong there, like a squatter: wrong beliefs that crowd out God's Word, or the world's influence on your children? Do you feel exposed, like a village with no walls, vulnerable and unprotected? Have you felt trampled like grain on a threshing floor, humiliated and walked over?

The Girgashites have been explained as dwellers in clay, a picture of living by the flesh, and the Amorites linked with speaking, even public slander. God promises to drive out every one, not by your effort, but as the ark goes before you. "You, O Lord, are a shield for me, my glory and the One who lifts up my head."

text: Your life doesn't have to be great to be beautiful. There's beauty in the small flower on the mountain.
explanation:
Everyone wants to be the majestic mountain; few notice the intricate flower growing on its slopes, or the gem lodged in a crevice. Fame isn't fulfilment. Solomon denied himself nothing, and concluded, "All was vanity and grasping for the wind." Many famous people live in polished prisons, unable even to walk down the street.

On holiday, Joseph Prince felt an unusual urge to go out alone for an evening walk. A woman recognised him in the park, and before they parted she had put her trust in Jesus. Whatever God has called you to, even if it seems small, do it for Him. "Whoever loses his life for My sake and the gospel's will save it."
